items.title: A smarter way to track and buy clean energy
items.summary: Learn how Google is scaling granular certificates to track clean energy hour by hour and support a cleaner, more reliable power grid.
items.body:
A smarter way to track and buy clean energy

Granular certificates are a next-generation tool to ensure more accurate, impactful clean energy buying.

Jenna Stauffer

Head of Strategic Priorities, Climate Operations

We are advancing Granular Certificates to track clean energy by hour and location, providing clear pricing signals that encourage smarter grid management. These tools help you match electricity use with local clean energy production, supporting a more stable power system. You can watch our new video to learn how these certificates help developers, energy asset owners, and the grid.

Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

• We use Granular Certificates to track clean energy supply by specific hour and geographic location.

• Trading volume in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region increased 437% during our recent monthly spot auctions.

• Our support for the Registry Acceleration Fund helps organizations verify and track hourly energy data.

• These certificates provide new revenue streams for battery storage operators and improve grid stability overall.

• We reduced our Scope 2 emissions by 3% while managing a 37% increase in electricity load.

Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

We are using new tools called Granular Certificates to track clean energy by the hour and location. These certificates help us match our electricity use with local solar or wind power, even when the sun is not shining. By creating clear price signals, this system encourages companies to build more batteries and clean energy projects where they are needed most. This helps us manage our power use and supports a cleaner, more stable energy grid.

Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

Explore other styles:

Granular Certificates (GCs) are next-generation clean energy instruments. They precisely track supply by hour and location, helping companies match their electricity load with local clean energy. Their hourly pricing signals encourage the development of clean generation and energy storage when and where it is needed most.

These instruments can incentivize improved grid management, and they can help accelerate the deployment of advanced clean technologies, leading to a cleaner, more stable power system. But like any nascent solution, the foundational building blocks need to be in place first.

We first started piloting GCs in 2021 and, in just five years, they’ve transitioned from early concept to real-world certificates, traded on specific hours. We’re continuing to take actions to accelerate both our own procurement and the global GC ecosystem.

Here are three key ways the GC ecosystem advanced this year:

1. The GC marketplace is growing.

Marketplaces are critical because they establish transparent hourly pricing signals and help simplify processes for those new to hourly procurement. LevelTen, in partnership with the Granular Certificate Trading Alliance (GCTA) and the Intercontinental Exchange, launched the Granular Certificate Marketplace in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic grid region PJM in October 2025. Since that first auction, trading volume has increased 437% in just one year, with Google participating in every monthly spot auction.

This increased trading volume generates clear pricing signals, with higher premiums occurring during evening hours. By demonstrating when buyers need clean energy most, GCs can incentivize suppliers to operate or build clean energy to meet this demand.

2. Global registries help with tracking and verification.

Almost every corporate clean energy buyer uses registries, which track and verify their clean energy purchases via instruments like monthly or annual energy attribute certificates (EACs). Registries help also ensure EACs are not double counted, supporting unique clean energy claims. However, until recently, the vast majority of registries didn’t have the technical capabilities to accommodate GCs.

To help address those gaps, Google supported the GCTA in establishing the Registry Acceleration Fund. The fund awarded grants to five of the largest organizations that operate registries, which collectively issue or track 4,000 TWh of certificates in over 70+ countries. As of today, one of these organizations has met their technical milestones that would allow them to transfer, verify, and retire GCs. The remaining four organizations are expected to finish in early 2027. This will add critical functionality needed for these instruments to scale, including standardization of the hourly data and traceability to one clear owner.

3. GCs are driving real value.

Despite the GC market’s nascency, its potential benefits are moving from academic research concepts towards demonstrating real impact. For example, in a recent GCTA white paper, clean energy developers and asset operators shared real-life perspectives on granular matching. These developers explained that pricing signals from GCs can help them maximize existing energy assets in the near-term, while helping them make crucial decisions about project siting and technology diversification in the longer term.

In addition, Google, esVolta, Quintrace, and LevelTen helped prove a new revenue stream for battery energy storage system operators. We partnered to pilot the first GCs for storage systems, shifting solar generation to match our targeted demand hours. This could not have happened without hourly tracking and verification via GCs.

Hear more firsthand accounts of the benefits of GCs to developers, energy asset owners, and the grid in our new video.

In addition to the maturing global ecosystem, we’ve also continued to evolve our use of GCs to help manage Google’s emissions. We’ll always prioritize applying new, long-term clean energy agreements, and the underlying hourly GCs, first.

Even with a large clean energy portfolio, the sun doesn’t always shine and the wind doesn’t always blow exactly when we need it to. Marketplace GCs help fill those gaps. At the same time, our purchases help build a stronger market where GCs can be bought and sold quickly, easily, and in large quantities — creating clearer price signals and providing granular options for growing numbers of buyers.

We used a smaller amount of marketplace GCs alongside a much larger amount of clean energy agreements to help lower our Scope 2 market-based emissions by 3% from 2024 to 2025, despite a 37% electricity load increase. We will include a limited amount of marketplace GCs in our 24/7 CFE performance in the future.

Looking ahead, these tools will become even more important to develop. The recently released net zero standard of the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) will require reporting on hourly matching performance for large energy users, and the GHG Protocol (GHGP) is evaluating the introduction of hourly emissions reporting. We will continue to work on developing and advancing GCs — not just for our own efforts, but to ensure others can use these tools to build a better energy system.

Small businesses, big results: How teams scale with AI

From faster sales replies to easier employee onboarding, explore easy ways to cut hours of manual work in Google Workspace — plus, free courses you can take today.

Yulie Kwon Kim

VP, Product, Google Workspace

These tools allow you to draft documents, organize data, and respond to inquiries faster so you can focus on growing your brand. Visit our Google Workspace AI resources page to explore these features and access training courses that help you get started with AI today.

• You can use Gemini in Gmail to draft replies, organize to-do lists, and manage customer inquiries.

• Our tools help you create training manuals, build production models, and brainstorm marketing campaigns with ease.

Behind almost every small business is a small team wearing every hat at once: running sales, marketing, and logistics on the shop floor — or on the go. When time and energy run short, scaling the business can seem like an impossible stretch. But driving big results shouldn’t require a big team or expensive software. With Google Workspace, AI is built into the apps you use every day, giving you an extra set of hands right where you work.

Here’s how four small businesses across the country use Google Workspace with Gemini to get busywork out of the way and get back to what matters most.

Bay Area Kids Rentals

When Tayo Lanlehin, a mom in Oakland, California, couldn’t find stylish, modern play equipment for her son’s first birthday party, she started Bay Area Kids Rentals. Logistics management is a huge part of her business, from loading delivery trucks to setting up events. Today, she uses Gemini in Gmail to help her be more efficient. She gets a daily brief of to-dos, pulls pricing from past files, and replies to inquiries in minutes instead of days. That speed has helped her close over 50% of incoming leads, double her revenue, and still make it home for dinner with her family.

Anderson Foundries

In Webster, South Dakota, husband-and-wife co-founders Kory and Ali Anderson are keeping 5,000-year-old metal casting techniques alive at Anderson Foundries. With veteran craftsmen retiring, Kory and Ali used Gemini Notebook to turn technical manuals into interactive training resources for new hires and apprentices. Beyond teaching the next generation, they use Gemini in Google Docs to draft complex quality manuals that keep their business compliant, a task that usually requires a specialized consultant. By drafting them with Gemini in-house, the team saves thousands of dollars and keeps its focus on the foundry floor.

Sourmilk

In 2025, when Elan Halpern’s homemade yogurt experiments outgrew her kitchen, she and her co-founder, Kiki Couchman, launched their probiotic Greek yogurt brand, Sourmilk. Often running the two-person business from their delivery bikes in New York City, they use Gemini in Google Sheets to help create production models and Gemini in Gmail to triage hundreds of email replies in minutes. With a little help from Gemini, the duo has been able to operate like a 10-person team and scale into more than 100 grocery stores within the brand’s first year.

Curious Elixirs

In New York’s Hudson Valley, former bar owner JW Wiseman and his team at Curious Elixirs have spent 11 years crafting booze-free, adaptogen-infused cocktails. Constantly jumping between the flavor lab, marketing, and operations, team members use Gemini in Google Docs to brainstorm marketing campaigns in their signature brand voice. They also rely on Gemini to generate styled product photos and source high-quality ingredient suppliers to keep production running smoothly.

AI for your business

You don’t need a massive budget or dozens of tools to put AI to work. These resources will help you get started.

• Google Workspace AI tools: Explore how built-in AI across Gmail, Google Docs, Sheets, Meet, and more can help your team save time on everyday tasks.

• Grow with Google AI training: Access Grow with Google resources that will help you reach more customers and streamline your work.

• Google AI Essentials course: Learn on your own schedule in courses taught by Google AI experts on using AI for daily tasks — no experience required.

• Free live workshops: Connect with a Grow with Google Coach or attend a virtual training for hands-on guidance.

items.title: Genie 4 is now available on the Gemini API.
items.summary: Build interactive 720p worlds with Genie 4 on the Google Gemini API. Generate coherent environments with native audio and real-time controls. Get started.
items.body:
Genie 4 is now available on the Gemini API.

Nov 19, 2026

Following yesterday's Genie 4 launch, Genie 4 is now available for developers through the Gemini API (via the Interactions API) and Google AI Studio.

Starting from a text prompt, a reference image, or both, developers can experiment with generating continuous 720p worlds at 24fps with synchronized native audio — from ambient soundscapes and sound effects to character dialogue. Using real-time keyboard controls alongside live text prompts, you can navigate environments and change weather, lighting, objects, or events on the fly. Gemini reasoning keeps the world state consistent and coherent throughout.

Whether you’re prototyping interactive experiences, visualizing designs for spatial concepts, or training robotics and AI agents, Genie 4 opens up a blank canvas for you to test ideas and define new possibilities. As a reminder every output includes imperceptible SynthID watermarking.

Try the interactive canvas and starter apps in Google AI Studio. Review pricing details and explore the Gemini API documentation to begin building.

This saves you time on the repetitive work that normally takes dozens of clicks. Just describe what you need, and Gemini handles the clicking, typing, menus, and forms for you.

Gemini works inside an isolated background window with a live preview right in your chat. Your main screen and cursor remain completely free, so you can keep typing, designing, or taking calls without interruption. Privacy and safety are built in: you choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen.

Here are a few ways you can start trying it today:

• Speed up creative workflows: Batch color-grade photos in your favorite design software or set up complex 3D scenes.

• Skip manual form entry: Extract weights, dimensions, and addresses from local PDFs to fill out multi-box shipping quotes.

• Turn live data into ready-to-present decks: Pull metrics and screenshots from live dashboards across multiple regions and build a presentation in Google Slides.

• Batch-list items for sale: Analyze clothing photos from a local folder, research pricing, log item details, and stage listings on resale platforms.

Computer use is rolling out in English in the U.S. in the Gemini app for Mac.

We are working with artists and musicians to test our Google Flow creative tools. Through Flow Sessions and Flow Music Sessions, we’re partnering directly with creatives to hear what matters most to them. This dialogue helps us build products that are useful, tailored to their work, and that helps enable creatives to build what they’ve been dreaming to build.

During our last six-week Flow Sessions, artists explored our AI creative studio, Google Flow. They developed visual projects, ranging from a pitch for a television series, animated shorts, and personal narratives, while experimenting with new workflows to see how our latest models can support their unique styles.

Today we’re sharing a look at the visual projects from this group of artists:

“A Lucky Greyhound” by Matias Collado

“Brood” by Siri Lee

“Roger & The Chicken” by River Davis

“UNFIXED” by Jeehyun Kim

“MIA” by Daniel Castro

“Reality Drop” by Johana Kroft

“How to Crack an Egg” by Luke Roberts

“Starling” by Ian Bradley

“The Catch” by Nate Talbot

In addition to the visual projects, for Flow Music Sessions, we brought together musicians and producers to take a similar approach to experimenting with new workflows and tools. They focused on Spaces, a feature within Google Flow Music, to create bespoke audio tools, plugins, mini music apps, new instruments, and digital artifacts that can be used directly in any creative workflow.

Check out the Spaces they created to get inspired, and you can try remixing their work to see how this approach can work for you:

Bloom Cycles: A vocal plugin that uses your webcam to shift your voice in real time based on your hand gestures.

Track Arranger: A songwriting tool that helps turn short loops into a full song structure with verses, choruses, and drops.

Mel’s Dreamscape Vocals: A bright, pop-focused vocal processor packed with pro presets and easy tuning tools.

Marble and Metal Visualisers: A 3D interactive visualizer that creates custom graphics reacting dynamically to live audio or uploaded music.

Tune Sampler: A vintage-style console plugin inspired by 90s hip-hop gear designed to shape audio with analog warmth.

Mirage Sampler: A playful software instrument that lets you easily drag and drop audio samples to flip them into unique textures and instruments.

We’re grateful for the opportunity to partner closely with such talented creatives, and learn how our tools can best support them. If you’re interested in participating in Flow Sessions, you can learn more here, and follow for updates on Flow Music Sessions.

Anthropic IPO料造就数百名亿美元富豪，员工人均持股价值约4400万美元

据《财富》报道，按 Anthropic 每股 83 美元的 IPO 发行价计算，公司 5300 名员工合计持有的股权估值约为 2320 亿美元，折合人均约 4400 万美元。

至少 400 名早期员工的身家将达到 1 亿美元或以上，其中部分人可能加入公司七名联合创始人的行列，成为亿万富豪。非创始人员工在首个交易日最多可出售个人持股的 10%，公司公布 2026 年业绩后，另有 35% 的个人持股将获得出售资格。

此次 IPO 对 Anthropic 的估值为 1.5 万亿美元，按上市估值衡量，规模位居历史第二，仅次于 SpaceX 的 1.77 万亿美元。不过，按募资额计算，Anthropic 的 810 亿美元超过了 SpaceX 的 750 亿美元。

七名联合创始人的持股比例相对均衡，预计每人的身家将大致翻倍至约 199 亿美元。七人均已承诺将个人所持 Anthropic 股权的 80% 用于慈善事业，相关承诺对应的价值可能超过 1000 亿美元。

与此同时，CEO Dario Amodei 曾在今年 1 月发表的文章中警告，AI 带来的巨额财富可能集中到足以破坏社会的程度。他将 AI 热潮与美国镀金时代相比较，认为处于 AI 经济繁荣前沿的人，应愿意放弃部分财富与权力，并向社会回馈。

items.title: Building the right way: Lessons from 20 years in The Dalles
items.summary: As our first data center in The Dalles, Oregon, turns 20, we’re looking back and announcing new investments in the local community.
items.body:
Building the right way: Lessons from 20 years in The Dalles

We’re celebrating the 20th anniversary of our first data center in The Dalles, Oregon.

Katy Bowman

Community Development Manager - The Dalles, Oregon

As we celebrate 20 years in The Dalles, Oregon, we are reflecting on our commitment to building data centers that support local jobs, infrastructure, and sustainability. To mark this milestone, we are launching a $10 million Energy Impact Fund and a new grant program for local organizations. You can read more about our history in the region and our future plans for the community on our official blog.

Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

• Katy Bowman reflects on twenty years of operating our first data center in The Dalles, Oregon.

• We have invested seven billion dollars in Oregon and supported local schools, fire, and rescue services.

• Our team prioritizes responsible growth through carbon-free energy, water conservation, and local infrastructure project funding.

• We are launching a new grant program and an energy fund to support our local neighbors.

Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

Katy Bowman, Community Development Manager in The Dalles, reflects on twenty years of operating our first data center in Oregon. We have invested over $7 billion in the region, supported local schools and fire services, and created thousands of jobs. By prioritizing water conservation, carbon-free energy, and community grants, we aim to be a responsible neighbor. We look forward to continuing this partnership and supporting the local economy for many years to come.

Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental.

Explore other styles:

In 2006, Google opened its first owned and operated data center in The Dalles, Ore. At the time, we didn't know whether it would grow beyond two small buildings with a few servers, let alone become the digital foundation for hospitals, banks, retailers, and other businesses in the region (and across the country).

Today, many of the innovations that shape how we approach data centers began there. As we mark this twenty-year milestone, we're reflecting on what we've built together with the local community, as well as what comes next.

Growing alongside Wasco County

Over these past two decades, Google has invested more than $7 billion in Oregon. As Wasco County's largest taxpayer in recent years, we help fund services like North Wasco County School District and Mid-Columbia Fire and Rescue. Throughout our time in Oregon, we’ve remained active members of the community: Googlers have volunteered more than 28,000 hours with nonprofits and schools around Oregon, while Google and its employees have given more than $35 million to organizations and nonprofits across the state.

In addition, for many families, our presence has meant building a career without leaving home. Over the last three years, our operations have supported an average of $862 million in state GDP each year. Our workforce in The Dalles spans a variety of backgrounds and includes a father-son duo, a pair of sisters, and many employees who have been with us for more than 15 years.

Googlers participate in a volunteer clean-up along The Dalles Riverfront Trail and Taylor Lake - 2025

Building the right way

Since we started building in The Dalles, we’ve worked to set the industry standard in developing data centers the right way. This means paying our own way, working to keep energy affordable, creating local jobs, showing up as active participants in our communities, and protecting shared resources like power and water.

Since 2022, our data centers in The Dalles have achieved more than 80% carbon-free energy — which we’re continuing to support through our 100 MW wind agreement with Avangrid and our 50 MW “superhot” geothermal deal with Quaise. We’ve also partnered with the Oregon Hazards Lab on wildfire prevention and Columbia Gorge Food Bank (CGFB) on hunger relief programs.

We recirculate cooling water at least 10 times before it leaves our facilities, so every gallon goes further — leaving more for farms, families, and businesses that share the watershed. In the last three years, we’ve spent more than $38 million on local water infrastructure and replenishment projects. This includes $28 million in funding for water and sewer infrastructure and an aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) system — a project that functions like an underground water savings account for the city. Upon completion, we transferred the ASR system and associated groundwater rights to the City of The Dalles. And we developed our third campus at a former Superfund site, previously home to an old aluminum smelter, which now provides a source of jobs and tax revenue for the county.

Looking ahead

To commemorate the anniversary, we're announcing two new programs in support of The Dalles:

• 20 for 20: Throughout 2027, we'll award $20,000 grants to 20 different organizations across Wasco County — one for each year we've called The Dalles home. These grants are not only our “thank you” to the local community, but also our commitment to continue supporting local organizations that help the region thrive.

• Energy Impact Fund: We're also launching a $10 million Energy Impact Fund to support energy affordability and efficiency for residents of the Columbia Gorge, with the first grant going to Energy Trust of Oregon.

Communities across the country are asking what it means to have a data center as a decades-long neighbor. The Dalles offers some insight: two small buildings became thousands of supported jobs, a lasting source of public revenue, and a local neighbor that is part of a thriving business community. To the people of The Dalles and Wasco County: a sincere thank you for having us as neighbors for the past 20 years. We're grateful for what we've built here, and we're committed to building responsibly together in the years ahead.

Katy Bowman, Community Development Manager in The Dalles, reflects on twenty years of operating our first data center in Oregon. We have invested over $7 billion in the region, supported local schools and fire services, and created thousands of jobs. By prioritizing water conservation, carbon-free energy, and community grants, we aim to be a responsible neighbor. We look forward to continuing this partnership and supporting the local economy for many years to come.

In 2006, Google opened its first owned and operated data center in The Dalles, Ore. At the time, we didn't know whether it would grow beyond two small buildings with a few servers, let alone become the digital foundation for hospitals, banks, retailers, and other businesses in the region (and across the country).

Today, many of the innovations that shape how we approach data centers began there. As we mark this twenty-year milestone, we're reflecting on what we've built together with the local community, as well as what comes next.
Growing alongside Wasco County

Over these past two decades, Google has invested more than $7 billion in Oregon. As Wasco County's largest taxpayer in recent years, we help fund services like North Wasco County School District and Mid-Columbia Fire and Rescue. Throughout our time in Oregon, we’ve remained active members of the community: Googlers have volunteered more than 28,000 hours with nonprofits and schools around Oregon, while Google and its employees have given more than $35 million to organizations and nonprofits across the state.

In addition, for many families, our presence has meant building a career without leaving home. Over the last three years, our operations have supported an average of $862 million in state GDP each year. Our workforce in The Dalles spans a variety of backgrounds and includes a father-son duo, a pair of sisters, and many employees who have been with us for more than 15 years.
Googlers participate in a volunteer clean-up along The Dalles Riverfront Trail and Taylor Lake - 2025

blocks.alt: Several Googlers picking up trash in The Dalles

blocks.text: Building the right way

Since we started building in The Dalles, we’ve worked to set the industry standard in developing data centers the right way. This means paying our own way, working to keep energy affordable, creating local jobs, showing up as active participants in our communities, and protecting shared resources like power and water.

Since 2022, our data centers in The Dalles have achieved more than 80% carbon-free energy — which we’re continuing to support through our 100 MW wind agreement with Avangrid and our 50 MW “superhot” geothermal deal with Quaise. We’ve also partnered with the Oregon Hazards Lab on wildfire prevention and Columbia Gorge Food Bank (CGFB) on hunger relief programs.

We recirculate cooling water at least 10 times before it leaves our facilities, so every gallon goes further — leaving more for farms, families, and businesses that share the watershed. In the last three years, we’ve spent more than $38 million on local water infrastructure and replenishment projects. This includes $28 million in funding for water and sewer infrastructure and an aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) system — a project that functions like an underground water savings account for the city. Upon completion, we transferred the ASR system and associated groundwater rights to the City of The Dalles. And we developed our third campus at a former Superfund site, previously home to an old aluminum smelter, which now provides a source of jobs and tax revenue for the county.
Looking ahead
To commemorate the anniversary, we're announcing two new programs in support of The Dalles:

items: 20 for 20: Throughout 2027, we'll award $20,000 grants to 20 different organizations across Wasco County — one for each year we've called The Dalles home. These grants are not only our “thank you” to the local community, but also our commitment to continue supporting local organizations that help the region thrive.

Energy Impact Fund: We're also launching a $10 million Energy Impact Fund to support energy affordability and efficiency for residents of the Columbia Gorge, with the first grant going to Energy Trust of Oregon.

blocks.text: Communities across the country are asking what it means to have a data center as a decades-long neighbor. The Dalles offers some insight: two small buildings became thousands of supported jobs, a lasting source of public revenue, and a local neighbor that is part of a thriving business community. To the people of The Dalles and Wasco County: a sincere thank you for having us as neighbors for the past 20 years. We're grateful for what we've built here, and we're committed to building responsibly together in the years ahead.

items.body:
Anthropic七位联创身家合计超1400亿美元

11 月 19 日，据彭博社报道，按 Anthropic 每股 83 美元的 IPO 发行价计算，七位联合创始人的身家合计超过 1400 亿美元，人均约 200 亿美元。彭博亿万富豪指数显示，七人按完全摊薄口径各持有约 1.3% 的经济权益。不到两年前，Anthropic 以 615 亿美元估值完成 35 亿美元融资后，七人首次跻身十亿美元富豪行列；今年 5 月完成另一轮融资后，七人全部进入彭博全球富豪榜前 500 名。

七名联合创始人在本次 IPO 中各出售约 338 万股，按发行价计算，每人出售的股份价值约 2.8 亿美元。CEO Dario Amodei 和董事长 Daniela Amodei 此前还参与了 2025 年 6 月和 2026 年 4 月的股份要约收购。其余股份仍受限售安排约束，联合创始人的限售期最长约一年，现任及前任员工最长约六个月。

尽管个人经济权益各约 1.3%，创始人仍通过 Founder LLC 持有一股 F 类普通股，在提交股东表决的一般事项上享有 50.1% 的投票权。招股书显示，2% 的持股门槛按每位创始人与其关联持有人在 IPO 完成时各自持有的 A 类股份计算，低于门槛的创始人将失去 Founder LLC 成员资格。七人还各自承诺将所持 Anthropic 股权的 80% 用于慈善事业，但这些承诺属自愿性质，可撤回，不具法律约束力。

Travis Beals

Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence

Nov 19, 2026

We’re partnering with Blue Origin on the first heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher, our long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit.

Targeted for Q1 2029, Blue Origin’s heavy-lift New Glenn rocket will deploy our satellites — each with roughly the capacity of a data center rack — into sun-synchronous orbit.

This dedicated launch builds on our ongoing work with other satellite and launch partners and represents a crucial milestone on our long-term roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute.

Anthropic IPO获约5000亿美元认购需求，指数基金首月或买入2.77亿股

11 月 19 日，据《金融时报》报道，尽管不少投资者对 Anthropic 的高估值、巨额资本开支和模型同质化风险存有疑虑，他们仍将其视为一只「必买股」。Anthropic 将 IPO 发行价定为每股 83 美元，高于此前 70 至 78 美元的区间，发行规模也从原方案上限约 640 亿美元扩大至约 810 亿美元，完全摊薄估值约为 1.5 万亿美元。承销商据悉获得约 5000 亿美元的认购需求，但认购订单可能被高报，不能等同于上市后的实际买盘。

Anthropic 是首家登陆公开市场、业务聚焦前沿 AI 模型开发的大型公司。投资者此前可通过谷歌、亚马逊等公司间接参与这一赛道，但这与直接持有 Anthropic 不同。对基金经理而言，即便对发行价有疑虑，若不配置而股价随后大涨，也可能面临业绩落后于同行的压力。

指数基金可能带来另一批买盘。Intropic 估计，若 Anthropic 符合相关指数的纳入条件，指数追踪基金可能在上市首月分四次买入约 2.77 亿股，相当于扩大后基础发行股数的约 28%。对这些基金而言，是否买入取决于指数规则，而非对估值的判断。

上市后也可能出现较大卖盘。部分非创始人内部人士最多可从首个交易日起出售所持股份的 10%，合计约 3.16 亿股，按发行价计算价值约 260 亿美元。这些股份具备出售资格，不代表持有人已经卖出。若首日表现强劲，部分获配基金也可能选择获利了结。

此外，同步进行的 260 亿美元私募配售包含芯片、算力和晶圆代工供应商。这些战略投资方一边向 Anthropic 投资，一边也是其基础设施开支的受益方，买入动机与普通基金不同。此次 IPO 能以更高价格扩大规模，并不意味着上市后仍有同样强的买盘；真正的考验是，尚未获配的投资者是否愿意在更高价位继续买入。

Anthropic前员工：Amodei曾谈公司未来可能比政府更强大，超级AI就像「魔戒」

Anthropic 即将上市，不少员工有望一夜暴富。但《纽约时报》采访发现，一些人眼下更关心的是：如果公司率先造出超级智能，究竟会获得多大的权力？

《纽约时报》专栏作者 Jasmine Sun 在过去两年采访了数十名 Anthropic 创始人、员工和离职者。一位匿名离职员工透露，CEO Dario Amodei 曾谈到，Anthropic 未来可能比政府更有权势，因此需要与各个国家建立自己的关系。

另一位离职员工则用《指环王》里的「魔戒」比喻超级智能。谁先造出来，谁就可能掌握最危险的网络武器、治愈各种疾病的方法，以及一支不知疲倦的 AI 大军。如此强大的力量一旦集中在少数人手中，掌握它的人是否值得信任，就变得至关重要。

Amodei 对这场竞赛的态度也发生了明显变化。2022 年，他曾公开表示，Anthropic 不应该抢跑，也不该训练远比同行更大的模型。当年，公司甚至因为安全顾虑，暂缓向公众推出 Claude，随后 OpenAI 凭借 ChatGPT 抢占了市场先机。

如今，Amodei 认为 AI 竞赛已经无法阻止。如果 Anthropic 不率先研发出最先进的模型，其他公司也会继续推进。只有保持领先，Anthropic 才有足够的影响力，推动整个行业采用更安全的做法。

这种使命感也深入了 Anthropic 的招聘流程。公司有一道著名的面试题：如果为了 AI 安全放慢研发，导致你的股票价值归零，你还愿意在这里工作吗？研究团队甚至会拒绝技术能力出众、但不认同公司理念的候选人。

随着公司快速扩张，内部开始出现分歧。一些早期员工担心，新加入的销售和市场人员只是冲着高薪与股票而来，未必真正相信公司的安全使命。还有员工主张立即停止训练更强的 AI，即使 OpenAI 等竞争对手不会跟着停，但遭到 Amodei 否决。

Anthropic 即将通过 IPO 获得巨额资金，继续购买算力、研发更强的模型。与此同时，公司还在争取国会给予反垄断豁免，以便未来能够与其他美国 AI 实验室协调放慢研发。

items.body:
OpenAI总裁Greg持有近300亿美元OpenAI股权，Sam后悔：当年该听他的

11 月 18 日，OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 和总裁 Greg Brockman 一同出席《纽约时报》DealBook 峰会。主持人 Andrew Ross Sorkin 当面提起两人的巨大财富反差：Greg 持有价值约 300 亿美元的 OpenAI 股权，Sam 却没有直接持股。

主持人问，这是否影响两人的关系？将来 OpenAI 上市，Sam 会不会也获得同等规模的股权？

Sam 表示，两人的关系完全没有受到影响，但没有回答自己未来是否会拿股权。

Greg 随后透露，当年筹划公司架构时，他曾明确建议 Sam 接受股权。这也是两人少有的分歧之一。但 Sam 坚持不拿，Greg 最终尊重了他的选择。

Sam 听完承认：「我当初真该听 Greg 的。」他还表示，不拿股权这件事后来给他带来了不少麻烦。

Sam 前不久刚解释过后悔的原因。今年 10 月，他接受《Vanity Fair》采访时表示，当初拒绝股权，是希望自己能够不受个人经济利益影响，为人类的未来做决策。但他发现，这个决定反而破坏了外界对他的信任。

他还曾公开抱怨，人们很容易理解一个 CEO 为赚钱而努力，却很难相信有人只是因为喜欢技术、希望影响技术和社会的发展，才如此投入工作。

谷歌推出Stitch Loop：AI全天盯着线上数据，自动找问题、改代码、验证效果

Google Labs 推出新实验产品 Stitch Loop，让 AI 智能体在软件上线后继续工作。原来的 Stitch 主要负责设计界面，新产品则能持续监测真实运营数据，发现问题、修改代码，再检查改动有没有效果。

开发者只需设定目标，比如提高购物网站的结账转化率。Stitch Loop 就会分析用户行为、运行日志和反馈，寻找影响转化的问题，提出改进方案。用户选定方案后，AI 会在隔离的云端环境中编写代码，提交 PR（代码修改请求），等待人工审核。

改动上线后，AI 还会继续追踪指标。如果效果不理想，就寻找下一轮改进机会。即使目标达成，也会持续监测，防止效果回退。

Stitch Loop 默认提供三类自动优化任务：网络安全、运行速度和无障碍适配。其中，安全任务结合 Gemini 4 Carbon 与 Google DeepMind 的 CodeMender，自动扫描代码漏洞并提出修复方案。

它支持连接 GitHub，通过 180 多种集成、MCP 和命令行工具获取产品数据，也能为 Antigravity 等编程智能体提供持续更新的产品上下文。

谷歌此前的 Jules 已能定期执行安全修补、性能优化等任务，但该产品已于 11 月 11 日转为只读，计划年底关闭。Stitch Loop 进一步把代码维护与真实业务指标结合起来。

目前 Stitch Loop 仍处于实验阶段，全球用户均可申请加入候补名单，符合条件的 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户享有优先体验资格。

Claude Code推出实验性Code Mode：一次调用多个工具，长任务可后台执行

Anthropic 为 Claude Code 加入实验性 Code Mode，已在 11 月 12 日发布的 v2.1.323 中上线，目前需要手动开启。

启用后，Claude 可以先编写 JavaScript 脚本，再通过脚本连续、并行调用多个工具，还能把工具返回的数据先处理好，只将必要结果交给模型，从而减少模型请求和 Token 消耗。

新模式还支持长时间任务在后台运行。Claude 可以一边执行命令，一边继续回答用户。官方文档显示，后台脚本最长可运行 2 小时，但需要使用 Auto 等自动授权模式。

Code Mode 由 Cloudflare 于 2025 年 9 月提出，Anthropic 同年 11 月也公开了类似方案。今年，DeepSeek Harness、Pi 和 OpenCode 2.0 等开源 Agent 框架陆续加入支持。

Anthropic 如今才将其集成进 Claude Code，目前仍处于实验阶段，需要手动开启。

OpenAI董事长创办的AI客服公司，半年估值拟翻倍至300亿美元

OpenAI 董事长、Salesforce 前联席 CEO Bret Taylor 创办的 AI 客服公司 Sierra，正洽谈融资约 15 亿美元，目标估值高达 300 亿美元。

Lightspeed、Greenoaks 和 Benchmark 正考虑投资，谈判仍处于早期。Sierra 今年 5 月刚以 158 亿美元估值融资 9.5 亿美元。仅过半年，估值就有望接近翻倍。

Sierra 成立于 2023 年，专门帮企业部署 AI 客服。它的智能体不仅能接听电话、回答问题，还能连接企业内部系统，处理退款、订单变更等事务。客户包括摩根大通、Cigna 等大型企业，部分业务按 AI 成功解决的问题收费。

它的收入增长也很快。Sierra 今年 10 月披露，年化经常性收入（ARR）已超过 4 亿美元，短短 5 个月翻了一倍。仅第三季度就新增超过 1.5 亿美元。按目前披露的收入规模计算，300 亿美元估值约相当于 ARR 的 75 倍。

竞争对手 Decagon 也在筹备新一轮数亿美元融资，其今年第二季度末年化收入约 1 亿美元，预计年底达到 1.75 亿至 2 亿美元。

OpenAI推出ChatGPT会计工作台：接入8款插件，帮企业对账、做报表

OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT for Accounting，发布专门的 Accounting 插件，并接入 QuickBooks、Xero、Oracle NetSuite、BILL 等 8 款合作插件，让 ChatGPT 可以直接读取企业账目，协助处理发票、银行对账、月末结账和审计准备工作。

过去，会计人员需要从邮箱、银行和财务软件中分别查找资料，再手工整理核对。现在，ChatGPT 可以汇集发票、银行流水和付款记录，识别交易金额、建议记账科目，再与账本逐笔核对，找出重复记账、遗漏交易及金额不符等问题。

到了月底，AI 还能按照企业原有的 Excel 模板编制财务报告，分析收入、支出等数据的变化，并附上对应的原始记录，方便会计人员核查。常用的报表格式、记账规则和检查步骤也可以保存下来，下个月继续使用。

Slack要做企业AI的指挥中心：让Agent接管任务，员工负责审核

Slack 宣布整合 Workflow Builder、Slackbot 和第三方 AI Agent，进一步将团队聊天工具升级为企业 AI 工作中枢。员工无需编写代码，就能在 Slack 中安排 AI 执行任务，并把处理结果接入现有业务流程。

比如员工提交 VPN 故障工单后，工作流可以直接唤起 IT Agent，带着问题继续排查。客户消息被标记后，Slackbot 能自动总结问题、起草回复。AI 生成的内容还可以经过人工审核，再写入 Jira、Google Sheets 或 Salesforce。

第三方 Agent 也有了自己的定时任务功能。用户只需保存一次指令，就能让已接入 Slack 的 Agent 每周自动整理销售机会、分析数据或生成报告，无需额外开发调度程序。
